chapter.heading: Tearing Down Barriers
chapter.v:
This is
me Paul, personally appealing to you through Christ's kindness and gentleness, the one who is “shy” when I have to face you but who is “bold” when I'm not there.

I'm pleading
with you, so that the next time I'm with you I won't have to be as tough as I think I'll have to be, boldly dealing with those who think we behave in worldly ways.

Even though
we live in this world, we don't fight as the world does.

Our weapons
are not of this world but God's mighty power that destroys fortresses of human thinking, demolishing misleading theories.

Every high
wall that stands tall and proud against the knowledge of God is knocked down. Every rebel idea is captured and brought into obedient agreement with Christ.

When you
are completely obeying Christ then we're ready to punish any disobedience.

Look at
what's staring you in the face! Anyone who considers that they belong to Christ should think again—just as they belong to Christ, so do we!

Even though
I may seem to be boasting a little too much about our authority, I'm not embarrassed about it. The Lord gave this authority to us to build you up, not to knock you down.

I'm not
trying to scare you by my letters.

People say,
“His letters are tough and severe, but in person he's feeble, and he's a useless speaker.”

People like
that should realize that what we say through letters when we're not there we will do when we are there!

We're not
so arrogant to compare ourselves with those who think so much of themselves. Those who measure themselves by themselves, and compare themselves with themselves, are really foolish!

But we
won't boast about ourselves in extravagant terms that can't be measured. We simply measure what we have done using God's system of measurement that he gave us—and that includes you.

We are
not over-extending our authority in saying this, as if we didn't get as far as you, for we did get to you and share with you the good news of Christ.

We're not
boasting in extravagant terms that can't be measured, claiming credit for what others have done. On the contrary, we hope that as your trust in God grows, our work among you will greatly increase.

Then we
can share the good news in places way beyond you, without boasting about what's already been done where someone else has worked.

“If anyone
wants to boast, boast about the Lord.”

It's not
those who praise themselves that are respected, but those that the Lord praises.
